A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same distributional reinforcement-learning study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison despite extensive rewriting, renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v5 reports original Atari and continuous-control experiments, including decomposition, DERAC sensitivity and entropy-interaction studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains original experimental results and reports additional evaluations, including the atom-count ablation in Appendix L.3.

M1.justification: Unlike v5 Section 5.2, v6 Equation 39 adds a cross-entropy-based bonus to DERAC's actor objective. Section 5.1 also revises DERPI's policy-improvement objective and places the Bellman bonus inside the next-state/action expectation. These change policy updates, although the categorical decomposition and interpolated critic loss remain.

E1.justification: v6 adds Pong in Figure 5's cross-entropy comparison. The original eight main Atari games and continuous-control environments remain represented across the paper.

E2.justification: v5 Figure 7 compares DERAC with AC, SAC and DAC(C51) on Humanoid and Walker2d; v6 Figure 6 drops SAC from these comparisons. The principal DQN/C51 and entropy-interaction comparator sets elsewhere are retained.

E3.justification: v6 introduces 20-, 80- and 100-atom configurations beyond the retained 51-atom setup and revises the epsilon/lambda combinations in DERAC's sensitivity study. The shared learning rates, batch size, discount factor and other Table 1 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v6 adds an atom-count ablation on Breakout and StarGunner, extends DERAC sensitivity testing to epsilon as well as lambda, and supplies the previously omitted C51 entropy-interaction analysis on BipedalWalkerHardcore. These broaden the investigation of discretization, parameter sensitivity and interacting regularizers.

E5.justification: v6 Figure 3 explicitly identifies shaded bands as standard deviations; corresponding v5 Figure 2 states averaging over three seeds without defining the bands. The established three-seed Atari and five-seed continuous-control reporting is retained.

E6.justification: Substantial result entries are added for Pong, multiple atom counts and C51 entropy interactions on BipedalWalkerHardcore. DERAC and actor-critic decomposition curves are also revised or replaced. Changed method and parameter conditions prevent interpreting these replacements as direct same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v6 adds a quantile-loss decomposition and approximate asymptotic mean-preserving argument in Section 7 and Appendix M. It also expands the KL argument, revises DERPI's assumptions and proofs, and changes the DERAC critic-loss derivation from an equality to an explicitly heuristic approximation.

C1.justification: v5 presents proposing an interpolating actor-critic algorithm as a headline contribution. v6 removes it from the contribution list and describes DERAC as a byproduct, emphasizing the intrinsic exploration benefits of categorical distributional loss. The central regularization-based explanation remains.

C2.justification: v6 develops excessive exploration as an explanation for DERAC's advantages, replacing v5's emphasis on distribution-information loss and recommendation to deploy DSAC. It also explicitly qualifies convergence by fixed q_theta, acknowledges heuristic loss simplification, and discusses restricted epsilon sensitivity and actor-critic instability.

D1.justification: Appendix K.2 adds the explicit conversion between the two epsilon parameters and probability-redistribution instructions. v6 also clarifies baseline implementations and identifies RLKit as the implementation platform, whereas v5 attributes implementation directly to Ma et al.'s source code. Most tabulated hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v6 substantially expands positioning around categorical learning and uncertainty-oriented exploration, including Farebrother et al. (2024), additional exploration literature and a dedicated Appendix A. It distinguishes the claimed intrinsic exploration effect from Bayesian, bootstrap, ensemble and distribution-based exploration strategies.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the explanatory prose are rewritten. v6 adds explicit motivation and outline passages, reorganizes the experiments, and consolidates DERAC's description, derivation and evaluations in Appendix J.

P2.justification: v6 adds a histogram-decomposition diagram, reorganizes entropy-interaction panels into benefit/interference groups, and merges or relocates DERAC figures. Numerous plots have revised legends, captions and arrangements, while Table 1 changes from vertically stacked blocks to a side-by-side layout.

improvement.justification: v6 adds useful sensitivity evidence, clearer implementation instructions and explicit qualifications of DERAC's guarantees. However, unlike v5, its expanded KL argument invokes Banach's fixed-point theorem after establishing only non-expansiveness (Appendix F.1, Equation 23), which does not justify the claimed uniqueness. This new theoretical reliability concern alongside the useful additions prevents a confident net quality judgment.
